Ameion / Nákyra (G52 ↔ G00)

Region (English scoring-table region): South Aelantir.

1444 starting country: Ameion (G52) Civil-war faction: Nákyra (G00)

One-sentence conclusion: Ameion is an atheistic civilisational expedition launched by an Alexander-like conqueror who knows the date of his death: you must sweep through Taychend before Laskaris's prophetic deadline, then use a republic, a vassal network, Kheionisation, archaeology, and two national crises to turn the conqueror's personal myth into an empire spanning South Aelantir.

Narrative: Extremely high | Mission-tree length: Very long (55 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: Current local files updated through 2026-07-09 | Distinctiveness: Extremely high | Waiting: Medium-high | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion capacity: Extremely high

Identity and History

Ameion (G52) lies on the Andic Reach of South Aelantir. In 1444 it is an Ambhen Kheionist republic, with Ameion as its capital and West Ovrestranan culture also accepted. It is not a suddenly appearing colonial state: the offline Wiki traces it to 684, when defeated Nékheis monarchists fled east with the remnants of their army. The city grew through trade linking Kheionai and Taychend, remaining distant from the Kheionai core while interacting with the peoples of Taychend and Devand. [Local history script] [Wiki source]

The opening ruler, Laskaris the Conqueror, is a 4/5/6 ruler and powerful general. He learned from the Weaver of Fate that he would not die before the age of 61; this is not immortality, but protection with a fixed expiry date. He used it to reform the army, intervene in Taychendi civil wars, and seize southern city-states. By 1444, Ameion is an outside order invading a warlord world, while Larankar's Erankar is becoming the other hero destined to collide with him. [Local history script] [Local event] [Wiki source]

Kheionism is not a traditional theistic faith but an atheistic philosophy of cities, republics, schools of thought, and state direction. Ameion nevertheless turns Laskaris's own political doctrine into a propagating and upgradeable “creed”, so the republic opposes god-kings while building a personal myth around a conqueror with a fixed destiny. That contradiction runs through the entire campaign. [Wiki source] [Local religion script]

National Story and Campaign Line

The first act is a race against death. Organise the Eucanthe alliance, reform the common army, secure the Muteba frontier, and advance along the southern coast of Taychend. The missions reinforce the military tempo while Laskaris lives; the “collision of destinies” with Erankar turns the two conquerors' war into the central heroic epic of the tree. [Local mission] [Local event]

The second act asks what keeps the country alive after the conqueror dies. Ameion turns Kheionai city-states into autonomous subjects or direct territory, transforms Taychendi soldiers into Fotistrépei who exchange service for land and status, and advances Kheionisation through education, intermarriage, conversion, and administration. In some regions the player can choose cooperation, autonomy, or coercive integration, but the main line never abandons its civilisational superiority: land is transferred from the disloyal to new soldiers, and a harsh labour system is revived. [Local mission] [Local narrative text]

The third act expands the empire throughout western Kheionai, northern Taychend, southern Chandya, and Iphilé. You build new cities and local capitals, contest sea power, organise colonial borders, investigate Precursor elven ruins, and finally claim the beginning of a “Second Age of Reflection”. This revival is not merely an archaeological hobby; it is Ameion declaring itself the political heir of the Precursors and imposing order across South Aelantir. [Local mission] [Local event]

The final crisis comes from inside the empire. The long conflict between republican and strongman traditions produces the Nákyran monarchists (G00); the player can remain G52 or switch to G00 and join a continental civil war, with both continuing to use the same 55 missions. An earlier coup event may also let Jaherios Lykos succeed, changing the country into Validaunéa (J99) and replacing the mission tree; that is an optional detour and not part of Ameion's continuous campaign chain. [Local event] [Local disaster script]

Core Mechanics

The destined conqueror. Laskaris is extraordinarily strong before the prophetic deadline, but the player must rapidly convert his personal advantage into territory, allies, and institutions; delay brings later wars and succession problems together. [Local history script] [Local event]

Populist and inheritance politics. The dedicated republican mechanic swings between republican tradition, taxation, and religious tolerance on one side and longer terms, aristocratic support, diplomatic prestige, and absolutism on the other; elections and events continually shift the balance. [Local government mechanic]

Kheionisation and the subject network. You can rule indirectly through autonomous city-states, garrison states, allies, and vassals, or pursue more concentrated and coercive cultural and religious integration. Expansion is not simple map-painting: it repeatedly asks who may enter the empire and in what status. [Local mission] [Local narrative text]

Precursor archaeology. Eligible ruins can be excavated with monarch points and time, progressively improving archaeological ability and searching for the lost floating city of Tasheni. The rewards can be powerful and permanent, but compete with conquest, technology, and stability for scarce points. [Local event] [Local modifier]

Multi-stage disasters. Political shocks after Laskaris's death, the later Nákyran civil war, and regional wars can split an established empire into factions again. The rework reduces the old tree's mechanical punishment, but still demands advance reserves of money, manpower, and fortifications. [Local event] [Local disaster script] [Community opinion]

Phased Play

Early game: attack continuously like Alexander. Use Laskaris and the mission-provided diplomatic relations to control southern Taychend quickly, but do not spend every monarch point on irrelevant development.

Mid game: institutionalise the conquests. Manage alliances and subjects, build cities, advance Kheionisation, and begin archaeology; this is the phase where war, points, culture, religion, and subject management all consume resources at once.

Late game: expand across South Aelantir, control sea power and trade, handle Iphilé, Chandya, and foreign Cannorian forces, and prepare for the Nákyran civil war. The country is strongest precisely when its territory is most vulnerable to being torn apart by crisis.

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 94/100 | Autocracy 65/100 | Magic↔Artifice 35/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; thematic intensity 82/100) | Pluralism 25/100.

The v2.1 value profile is Neutral (47/100) with a branch-dependent trajectory. Kheionisation, cultural and religious assimilation, and the imperial civilisational mission first produce a more uniform society; land seizure, labour, and coercive transformation further reduce the value score, while the state also provides city-building, stability, limited autonomy, and avenues of advancement for the conquered. Imperial expansion itself is not counted twice as evidence of evil.

Recommended for players who enjoy a powerful character opening, rapid conquest, subject politics, archaeology, civilisational revival, and a major civil war. Avoid it if you dislike deadlines, resource gates, cultural assimilation, long multi-front wars, or playing an imperial protagonist rather than an egalitarian liberator.

Community Experience

[Community opinion] A 2025 rework experience post generally praises the new tree's tempo, Laskaris events, religious and cultural conversion, and subject management over the old version; it still warns that the early economy is tight and monarch points are precious, making sustained war the smoothest approach. Player experience post

[Community opinion] Another comparison describes Ameion as high-intensity expansion followed by slower assimilation and integration, and praises its writing; it also notes that a large Taychend conquest is hard to avoid. This describes player feel, not current mechanics. Comparison discussion

Evidence Boundary

This article covers the base Mod and translation v1.37.5.0, checked on 2026-09-23. G52's identity, 55 direct missions, shared G00 missions, the J99 detour, political mechanics, archaeology, and civil war come from current local files.

The complete offline Wiki snapshot is available. This article reads Republic of Ameion (page_id=749, revision_id=31892), Wars of Two Heroes (3938/31754), and Kheionism (1545/32062) for history and setting only. Full records of official development material and the two player sources are on the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

Native English national-idea names and descriptions are reproduced below with the inherited effect displays. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Alternative sets and successor ideas do not automatically stack. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals, not events already completed in 1444. Native English wording is reused rather than back-translating embellished Chinese localisation. Inherited display-unit assumptions remain unverified; this translation does not correct source data.

Ameion (G52) — Ameioni Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
        tag = G52
    }

Traditions: Ameioni Traditions

Effects: Discipline: +5%; Colonists: +1.

Idea 1: Laskaris the Conqueror

For a long time Ameion was in isolation, focused on building a worthy capital and slowly colonizing its surroundings. In that age, we were nothing more than a peripheral state; forgotten to the world.

This all changed with the rise of Laskaris, a mighty elf and a brilliant speaker, who learned the time of his demise, effectively giving him immortality before his deathday. Using this, he got himself elected and became the leader of Ameion. He renovated the army and navy, and led them on a path of conquest through Taychend; his ultimate goal being the seizure of the jewel of Taychend, the great city of Nanru Nakar, Nákyra in Kheionai.

His victories gave us a presence in Taychend, but there is still much to be done. Even now, rebels and warlords conspire against us; threatening to push us back into the sea. But this will never occur, for one day Laskaris’ dream will be realized, and all of Taychend will fall under our dominion.

Effects: Province warscore cost: -15%.

Idea 2: Healing Wounds

Many centuries ago a movement grew among the Nékheis, conspiring to kick out their Alecandi overlords and establish a great kingdom of cities in Devand. The subsequent war that followed would see these heroes defeated, chased to the edge of the known world. Tired and exhausted, they finally settled down near where a great river emptied into the sea, and this settlement would eventually grow into a grand city; known to us as Ameion.

At last, we re-established contact with our cousins to the west. Although much bad blood remains between us, it is prudent that we mend these old wounds. Our diplomats have been slowly but steadily restoring ties with the other Kheions, learning many tricks to appease their leaders in the process.

Effects: Improve relations: +20%.

Idea 3: Kheionization

The Taychendi are an odd people, so similar, yet so distinct from our own. They live in city states, yet bend the knee to monarchs. They practice agriculture, yet also feel the need to raid eachother’s lands constantly. They produce great philosophers and writers, yet worship dead rulers as gods.

Their history is tragic, a constant cycle of conflict, consolidation, and collapse; repeating continuously since the Erriphi and bringing only suffering and chaos in its wake. As far as the Taychendi are concerned, we are merely the next in a long series of conquerors seeking to rule Taychend.

Our philosophers have determined that it is the Taychendi belief system, that of god-heroes and divine kings, that is the source of Taychend’s misery. We will institute a great program to "Kheionize" the Taychendi. By education, policies, and intermarriage, the Taychendi will become properly civilized; and the cycle of warlordism will meet its end under Kheionai guidance.

Effects: Culture conversion cost: -10%; Missionary strength: +1%.

Idea 4: Fotistrépei Regiments

One of the policies introduced to further the Kheionization of the Taychendi was the Fotistrépei System. Taychendi soldiers serving in the Ameioni army, who willingly adopted Kheionai culture and became Kheionized, would receive land and privileges from Ambhen administrators; which were often seized from disloyal Taychendi nobility and peasantry. These soldiers, known as Fotistrépei, formed a permanent and loyal native force, whose existence and status was tied to the success of the Ameioni Empire. The Fotistrépei would form one of the core groups of the emerging Klereyen culture that developed in the 1500s and were instrumental in the rise of the Klereyen within Ameioni society.

Effects: Manpower from true faith provinces: +20%.

Idea 5: Revive the Eisphoráth

In the years following the exile of our ancestors, they underwent numerous hardships building a society from nothingness. They were forced to create a functioning and stable state with what few resources they had and, unlike the Nékheis, had no aid from our cousins to the west.

Of the systems that developed during this dark period of isolation, Eisphoráth was the harshest. Disregarding its strictness, it was a well run and advanced system of labor and resource management, invented to ensure all contributed their dues to ensure the survival of the settlement. This system was abandoned over time, as the need for it disappeared with the reestablishment of trade links to the rest of the world.

As our consolidation of Taychend continues, many of our officials have begun to look to the past for inspiration to solve our current issues with the Taychendi not cooperating. It is about time we reintroduce the Eisphoráth, for only with a harsh system like this will the Taychendi be coerced into properly contributing to our empire.

Effects: Development cost: -10%.

Idea 6: The Ýmytolí

The Ýmytolí are a series of fortifications created to repress the ever present rebels that hide among the various hills of Taychend. Built in strategic positions that not only offer great defensiveness but also easy access to supply lines and reinforcements, the Ýmytolí are always kept in perfect condition.

Effects: Fort maintenance: -15%.

Idea 7: Deny The Cannorians

At first there were few. A small group of ships, explorers from a faraway continent beyond Aelantir. But this trickle turned into a flood, as all sorts of foreign people of differing colors and sizes crowded our Taychendi ports, seeking to steal the valuable relics of our ancestors.

At first, they were tolerated. But soon, our local administrators placed restrictions on their movement and influence. Once our agents learned of Cannorian companies supplying Taychendi rebellions against us, the decision was clear. The Cannorians were barred from our ports for good and we sent our fleet to stop the Cannorians from ever reaching Taychendi shores. Unfortunately, the Cannorian greed for ancient elven relics was so great, that smugglers soon appeared to meet their demand…

We face a constant struggle against the Cannorians, who seek to bring down our empire to satisfy their greed. We will not let their wishes be realized for we are inheritors of the Precursor legacy; and we will not let the foreigners defile it.

Effects: Ship trade power: +10%; Naval Morale: +10%.

Ambition: Ameioni Ambition

Effects: Reserves Organisation: +15%.

Nákyra (G00) — Nákyran Ideas

Effects: Discipline: +5%; Colonists: +1.

Effects: Province warscore cost: -15%.

Idea 2: The Cult of Laskaris

Laskaris the conqueror came to Taychend in a great effort to bring the benefits of civilization. His heroic actions saved them from the barbarity and warlordism they were so accustomed to. Since his prophesized passing, a cult grew around the worship of him and his descendants among the Taychendi, who see him and his bloodline as divine. And among those that did not see his bloodline as divine, they certainly venerated the principles Laskaris and his descendants would espouse: populism.

Thirendires, a descendant of Laskaris, would rise to power with the support of the Laskarian cult and the common people behind him. He ascended to kingship, proclaiming that the people have elected the bloodline of Laskaris as the rulers of these lands. The great rebellion that followed by those still believing in the philosophized ideal of a republic was crushed, and Thirendires proclaimed a new populist and Monarchist era for the world of the Kheionai.

Effects: Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Horde unity: +1; Religious unity: +20%.

Idea 3: Emulating the Precursors

The large archeological program conducted by the Nákyran Empire led to the rediscovery of ancient Precursor building techniques and styles, which the Laskaris dynasty embraced wholeheartedly as the new official building style of the empire. A large building spree would ensue, with every city in every region of the empire having constant construction projects built in the precursor style and old buildings being renovated to emulate them.

Effects: Construction cost: -10%.

Idea 4: Klereyen in the Government

The Klereyen are the Taychendi that have embraced civizilation and the ways of the Kheionai. Even still, they were not properly integrated into the government of Ameion. This changed with the ascension of Thirendires to kingship, with the Klereyen as his most loyal followers. He rewarded them by putting them in the highest levels of administration and favoring them as such. In every part of the empire of Nákyra, the Klereyen can be found, a policy continued by Thirendires's successors, who saw the Klereyen as their most loyal base of support.

Effects: Ruler culture advisor cost: -15%; Culture conversion cost: -15%.

Idea 5: The Krypharpedan

Even after their defeat on the field of battle, many Kheionai still cling to their philosophized ideal of a republic. While many among them are too disheartened to continue resistance, many more refuse to acknowledge, and actively resist the truth: the blood of Laskaris are the rulers of these lands. The lingering resentment and occasional rebellion against the monarchy has led to the need to create a new force designed specifically to combat this ever present threat: The Krypharpedan.

Recruited from amongst the most loyal of Klereyen, they actively hunt the republican resistance. Especially active in the Devand and in the kheions, they are the shield that keeps the royal family, and Nákyra as a whole, safe from both domestic and foreign attack.
